policy: Field entries are published work that changed how AI systems are built. Each cites its primary record (an arXiv first version or a dated announcement) and names the catalog roles it shaped; the date is that record's date, not a claim about who was first. Our entries are contribution hypotheses: each names the files that implement it, the evidence for its present status and an experiment that could falsify it. Novelty is unassessed for every one of them; none is a patent, first-of-its-kind or proven-return claim. arXiv records were matched by identifier, title and first author against a research index on the check date.

statuses.title: Implemented
statuses.meaning: Runs in this repository and is covered by a test or gate.

statuses.title: Partial
statuses.meaning: Part of the mechanism runs; the evidence named is incomplete.

field.name: Hierarchical navigable small-world graphs

arxiv.title: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search using Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs

field.consequence: Graph-based approximate nearest-neighbour search became the default index inside vector stores, which is what makes embedding retrieval practical at corpus scale.

field.name: The Transformer

arxiv.title: Attention Is All You Need

field.consequence: Self-attention replaced recurrence, so training parallelised across sequence positions; every model the catalog routes to descends from this architecture.

field.name: Bidirectional pre-trained encoders (BERT)

arxiv.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

field.consequence: Pre-training an encoder once and fine-tuning it per task made pre-trained encoders the starting point for search, classification and extraction; the retrievers in this register build on them.

field.name: Sentence embeddings for similarity search

arxiv.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks

field.consequence: Siamese training produced sentence embeddings comparable by cosine similarity, which made embedding a corpus once at ingest time and searching it by vector a practical pipeline.

field.name: Neural scaling laws

arxiv.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

field.consequence: Loss was shown to fall predictably with parameters, data and compute, which turned model training into a capital-planning problem and explains why most teams buy models rather than train them.

field.name: Dense passage retrieval

arxiv.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering

field.consequence: Learned dual encoders retrieved passages that keyword search missed, establishing embeddings computed at ingest time as a retrieval baseline.

field.name: Late-interaction retrieval (ColBERT)

arxiv.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT

field.consequence: Token-level matching after independent encoding sits between single-vector search and full cross-encoder re-ranking, and is the usual reference for multi-vector retrieval.

field.name: Retrieval-augmented generation

arxiv.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

field.consequence: Separating what the model knows from what the corpus says made answers citable and corpora updatable without retraining; it is the basis of the catalog's cite-or-refuse contract.

field.name: In-context learning at scale

arxiv.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners

field.consequence: Tasks could be specified with instructions and examples in the prompt instead of a fine-tuned model, which made the prompt an application artifact to version and test.

field.name: Sparse mixture-of-experts at scale

arxiv.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity

field.consequence: Routing each token to one expert decoupled parameter count from per-token compute, so model size stopped being a reliable proxy for serving cost.

field.name: Low-rank adaptation

arxiv.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

field.consequence: Training small low-rank updates on a frozen model made adapters cheap to train, store and swap per tenant or task.

field.name: Chain-of-thought prompting

arxiv.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models

field.consequence: Asking for intermediate steps improved multi-step answers, and spending tokens on reasoning became a cost and latency decision an architect has to make explicitly.

field.name: Instruction following from human feedback

arxiv.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

field.consequence: Fine-tuning on demonstrations and human preference rankings produced models that follow instructions, the behaviour every assistant product now assumes.

field.name: Self-consistency decoding

arxiv.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models

field.consequence: Sampling several reasoning paths and taking the majority answer trades extra calls for reliability, and the agreement rate doubles as a cheap uncertainty signal.

field.name: IO-aware exact attention

arxiv.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness

field.consequence: Tiling attention around GPU memory movement cut its memory footprint without approximation, which is part of why long context windows became affordable to serve.

field.name: Interleaved reasoning and acting (ReAct)

arxiv.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

field.consequence: Alternating thoughts with tool calls and observations gave the agent loop its common shape: decide, act, read the result, decide again.

field.name: Speculative decoding

arxiv.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding

field.consequence: A small draft model proposes tokens that the large model verifies in parallel, lowering latency while keeping the large model's output distribution.

field.name: Constitutional AI

arxiv.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

field.consequence: Written principles plus model-generated critiques replaced much of the human labelling for harmlessness, making a policy document part of the training input.

field.name: Self-taught tool use

arxiv.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

field.consequence: A model learned when to call an API and how to use the result, framing tools as something a model chooses rather than something a pipeline forces.

field.name: Indirect prompt injection

arxiv.title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection

field.consequence: Instructions hidden in retrieved or tool-returned content can steer the model, so every retrieved document and tool result is untrusted input and tool authority must be bounded outside the model.

field.name: Verbal self-reflection (Reflexion)

arxiv.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning

field.consequence: Agents that write down why an attempt failed and read it on the next attempt improve without weight updates, which makes episodic memory a design element.

field.name: Tree of thoughts

arxiv.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models

field.consequence: Exploring and pruning several partial solutions turns reasoning into a search an orchestrator can budget, with an explicit trade between calls and quality.

field.name: Quantized low-rank adaptation

arxiv.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs

field.consequence: Training adapters on a quantized base model brought fine-tuning of large open models within reach of a single accelerator.

field.name: Direct preference optimization

arxiv.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model

field.consequence: Preference tuning without a separate reward model or reinforcement-learning loop made it a supervised training job that more teams can run.

field.name: Model-graded evaluation

arxiv.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena

field.consequence: Strong models agree with human preference often enough to grade open-ended output, and they carry measurable position and verbosity biases, so a judge is itself something to calibrate.

field.name: Position sensitivity in long context

arxiv.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts

field.consequence: Models used information at the start and end of a long context more reliably than the middle, so the order and size of retrieved context are design parameters, not details.

field.name: Paged attention for serving (vLLM)

arxiv.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention

field.consequence: Managing the attention cache in pages, like virtual memory, let servers batch far more concurrent requests and set the template for open-source model serving.

field.name: Reference-free retrieval evaluation (Ragas)

arxiv.title: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation

field.consequence: Faithfulness, answer relevance and context relevance became separate metrics, so a failing retrieval system can be traced to the retriever or the generator.

field.name: Graph-based retrieval over community summaries

arxiv.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization

field.consequence: Building an entity graph and summarising its communities at ingest time answers corpus-wide questions that chunk retrieval cannot, at the cost of a heavier ingest pipeline.

field.name: Function calling in a model API
field.consequence: Models emitted structured calls against developer-declared schemas, moving tool use from prompt parsing into the API contract.

field.name: Schema-constrained output
field.consequence: Constraining generation to a supplied JSON Schema turned output validation from a retry loop into a guarantee of the decoding step.

field.name: Model Context Protocol
field.origin: Anthropic; donated to the Agentic AI Foundation
field.consequence: One open protocol for exposing tools, resources and prompts to any model client replaced per-integration adapters; it underlies the catalog's tool hub pattern.

field.name: Agent2Agent protocol
field.origin: Google; moved to the Linux Foundation
field.consequence: Agents built on different frameworks can discover each other's capabilities and exchange tasks, the agent-to-agent counterpart to MCP's agent-to-tool interface.

ours.name: Experience-to-topology compiler
ours.mechanism: One pattern file holds the customer journey, component IDs and flows; the compiler emits React Flow, Mermaid, diagrams.net, SVG and Structurizr views that share those IDs, so no view is drawn by hand.
ours.evidence: Tests assert identical component and flow IDs across views and byte-identical output for identical input.
ours.experiment: Give two teams the same change request, one editing hand-drawn views and one editing the pattern file; compare drift between views and time to a consistent set.
ours.prior_work: Architecture-as-code tools, the C4 model and Structurizr, model-driven engineering.

ours.name: Evidence-preserving portal
ours.mechanism: Every maturity the portal displays must be backed by an artifact-specific receipt; the compiler refuses to promote a fixture beyond 'visualized' or import runtime receipts.
ours.evidence: The compiler rejects runtime maturity and receipts in fixtures. No live receipt has been recorded, so promotion with real evidence is untested.
ours.experiment: Hand a reviewer contradictory receipts and measure how often a higher maturity is displayed than the receipts support.
ours.prior_work: Software supply-chain provenance (SLSA, in-toto), evidence-based assessment.

ours.name: Dual value ledger
ours.mechanism: Customer value counts only accepted results, while cost counts every attempt; the provider's consumption drivers are shown beside it and never move the customer score.
ours.evidence: The economics function and its test charge failed attempts. The figures are assumptions per pattern; no pilot data exists.
ours.experiment: Run one pilot with the ledger and one without; compare whether scope decisions improve net customer value without consumption that buys no accepted result.
ours.prior_work: Unit economics, FinOps cost allocation, value-stream measurement.

ours.name: Source-drift gate
ours.mechanism: Every product and program claim carries a checked-on and review-by date; the compiler stops when one passes, so stale claims cannot be published.
ours.evidence: A test proves compilation fails on an expired source. The gate does not yet list which pages, templates or chapters depend on the expired claim.
ours.experiment: Expire one API claim and measure how many dependent artifacts a maintainer finds with and without a generated dependency list.
ours.prior_work: Documentation linting, dependency freshness bots, citation management.

ours.name: Portable acceptance capsule
ours.mechanism: Tests, results, ownership and rollback steps are exported with the solution so a customer can re-run acceptance on their own host.
ours.evidence: The practice domain runs against a synthetic fixture only; no customer host has reproduced a capsule.
ours.experiment: Reproduce one capsule on a fresh customer host and record every manual step needed.
ours.prior_work: Reproducible builds, acceptance-test-driven development, release evidence packs.

ours.name: Industry R&D workbench
ours.mechanism: Evidence-linked industry cases generate solution variants and lab missions from the same catalog.
ours.evidence: Described in this register only; nothing runs.
ours.experiment: Compare time to a reviewable design against an existing discovery workflow on the same brief.
ours.prior_work: Design-space exploration tools, pattern languages, case-based reasoning.

ours.name: One answer contract on three runtimes
ours.mechanism: A single cite-or-refuse contract module is copied verbatim into the Vercel, Cloudflare and Cloud Run templates, and one conformance suite runs against all three.
ours.evidence: The sync check fails when a template's copy drifts, and conformance tests run locally. No provider deployment receipt exists.
ours.experiment: Deploy all three and run the conformance suite against each live endpoint; record any behaviour that differs by runtime.
ours.prior_work: Consumer-driven contract testing, OpenAPI conformance suites.

ours.name: Reweightable judgement scorecard
ours.mechanism: Each realization carries a recorded 1-to-5 judgement per criterion with a written rationale, published per criterion so a reader can reweight them; no score is presented as a benchmark, and provider consumption never changes a customer score.
ours.evidence: Validation rejects scores outside 1 to 5 and realizations without a rationale.
ours.experiment: Ask several architects to score the same realizations independently and measure agreement before publishing a ranking.
ours.prior_work: Multi-criteria decision analysis, architecture trade-off analysis (ATAM).

ours.name: Verified-icon rule
ours.mechanism: Official vendor icons are embedded only from a hash-pinned registry and only for that vendor's services; every other node uses a neutral role glyph.
ours.evidence: The compiler fails on a hash mismatch or on an official icon attached to another provider's service; a test covers the second.
ours.experiment: Audit a sample of generated diagrams against vendor icon terms and count misattributed marks.
ours.prior_work: Vendor icon kits and their usage terms, asset provenance in design systems.

ours.name: Name-evidence ledger
ours.mechanism: Every service name carries how it was verified (a registered source, a long-standing name, or inferred from a rename); inferred or non-GA names are flagged to confirm before customer use.
ours.evidence: Validation requires registered sources for source-verified names, and each realization lists the bindings to confirm.
ours.experiment: Re-check flagged and unflagged names against vendor documentation and compare the error rate of each group.
